mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a flat or declining housing starts series (HOUST) indicates a divergence between income growth and capital expenditure, suggesting pent-up savings and reduced investment, which leads to muted S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM and HOUST <= 0% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 3.5% for four consecutive months, coupled with a simultaneous decline in industrial production, signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 3.5% for 4 consecutive months AND INDPRO < 0% for the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than GDPC1 quarter-over-quarter) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS QoQ growth exceeds GDPC1 QoQ growth for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered quarters.
